title: Queued Latency Fence and Implicit Kernel Probing
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Background: We observe intermittent tail spikes (~p99) when queues mix short-prefill requests and long-prefill streams on heterogeneous hardware. Root causes identified in recent traces: (1) bursty queue depth exceeding the kernel's optimal launch configuration, (2) last-minute kernel variant switches that incur warm-up overhead, and (3) brittle admission rules that allow coarse-grained merging of incompatible sequences.

Goal: Reduce tail latency by introducing a lightweight admission 'latency fence' that caps effective queue depth per slot for latency-sensitive requests and an implicit kernel probing mechanism that opportunistically predicts the most efficient kernel variant for an incoming request before decode starts. The solution should be low-overhead, safe to enable behind a feature flag, and compatible with existing batching and KV-cache behavior.

High-level approach:
- Latency fence: introduce a soft cap on admission that biases short/latency-sensitive requests into earlier dispatch cycles when queue depth is high. The fence is a configurable policy with three operating modes (off, conservative, aggressive) and a per-tenant override.
- Implicit kernel probing: piggyback a tiny telemetry probe on admitted requests (sampling <= 5% of traffic) to run a micro-benchmark of candidate kernels on the per-GPU queue thread and record expected execution times for the request's token-length/profile. Use the probe signal to pick kernel variants for subsequent requests with similar shapes.
- Batch shaping integration: augment the batch shaper to consider fence metadata and probe-derived kernel affinity when forming dispatch batches, preventing mixing of incompatible kernel shapes in the same dispatch where it would induce latency amplification.
- Safety: ensure probes are always non-blocking and can be throttled. Rollout behind a canary gate; provide automatic rollback if p99 increases.

Deliverables: feature flag, admission policy config, kernel-probe sampler, batch-shaper hook, metrics dashboards, canary runbook, and docs for ops and PMs.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end canary shows at least 30% reduction in p99 for mixed short/long workload compared to baseline under target load
No regression in p50 or throughput (>98% of baseline) for throughput-first tenants
Kernel variant selection converges for sampled shapes within one minute in 95% of probes
Feature gated and instrumented: flag, probe-rate config, per-tenant mode, and automatic rollback configured
Unit and integration tests for admission fence and probe sampler added to CI
